summary: mountainash-auth-client is built around a discriminated-union type system with pluggable dispatch, protocol-based extensibility, and a clear separation between auth schemas, protocol flows, connection lifecycle, and credential persistence. Key architectural seams -- the AuthSpec subclass hierarchy, AUTH_TO_DRIVER_KWARGS registry, SecretStore protocol, and spec/metadata convention -- allow each layer to evolve independently while keeping the overall design cohesive.
use_cases: Evaluate how the discriminated-union pattern and dispatch registry support adding new auth strategies with minimal coupling
Understand the token lifecycle state machine and how file-locked refresh prevents concurrency issues
Assess the SecretStore protocol as an integration point for enterprise credential backends
Review the spec/metadata convention that decouples OAuth flows from provider-specific configuration

concepts.name: Discriminated Union + Dispatch Pattern
concepts.description: AuthSpec subclasses use a Literal 'kind' discriminator to form a closed union of auth strategies. The AUTH_TO_DRIVER_KWARGS registry maps auth types to callable mappers that produce driver-ready keyword arguments. Some auth types intentionally have no default mapper, signaling that backend-specific handling is expected -- a deliberate design choice that keeps the dispatch layer honest about what it can generalize.

concepts.name: Spec/Metadata Convention
concepts.description: Provider configuration is carried by spec objects exposing a .name identifier and a .metadata dictionary containing flow-specific URLs, flags, and settings. OAuth2 metadata includes authorize_url, token_url, use_pkce, default_scope, and callback_port. OAuth1 metadata carries request_token_url, authorize_url, and access_token_url. Mixins reference specs via a _spec ClassVar set at class definition, keeping provider config static and declarative.

concepts.name: OAuth2 Flow with PKCE
concepts.description: Implements the Authorization Code grant with S256 PKCE code challenge generation, synchronous token exchange via httpx, refresh with automatic fallback to full re-authorization, and expiry checking with a configurable buffer window. The flow is designed to be composable -- usable standalone or through the connection mixin.

concepts.name: Token Lifecycle State Machine (Mixin)
concepts.description: The connection mixin manages five token states: no-token, valid-token, expired-with-refresh, expired-no-refresh, and cleared. The connect() method walks a decision tree that loads stored tokens, checks expiry, acquires a file lock for concurrent-safe refresh, and falls back to re-authorization when needed. A one-time migration path moves inline profile tokens to the credential store.

concepts.name: SecretStore Protocol + Filesystem Backend
concepts.description: A runtime-checkable Protocol defining six methods for credential persistence, with a production-ready filesystem backend. The filesystem store uses a domain/provider/user three-level key space, YAML serialization, restrictive permissions (0o600 files, 0o700 directories), symlink rejection, atomic writes via temp-file-and-replace, tombstone-based clear tracking to prevent re-migration, and fcntl exclusive file locking for concurrent refresh safety.

concepts.name: Optional Dependency Boundary
concepts.description: OAuth1 support depends on authlib, managed as an optional dependency with a clear import boundary. OAuth1 modules use deferred imports with descriptive ImportError messages, and are intentionally not re-exported from the package root -- keeping the default install lightweight while making the upgrade path straightforward.
